title: The Last Password
script: What if the last password you remembered was already behind you? Passkeys already replace passwords in supported services. Imagine that same ease at your office, your hotel, and your front door. Every entrance works, until one account stops recognizing you. Convenience starts looking like infrastructure when losing access means losing your day. When passwords disappear, who holds the key?
timingStatus: Estimated silent editorial timings. Refit scenes and caption timestamps to the unchanged voice-over when supplied.
concept: Passkeys and selective digital identity make login invisible, but identity becomes infrastructure.
whyNow: A present capability creates a plausible human decision; this is a scenario, not a forecast.
viewerGoal: Consider the human consequence and choose a boundary.
hooks: What if the last password you remembered was already behind you?
Your front door works like a login now.
Losing one account could lock you out of your day.
strongestHook: What if the last password you remembered was already behind you?
directorBrief: Direct this as a human story about Passkeys and selective digital identity make login invisible, but identity becomes infrastructure. Emotional movement: ease → dependence. Open with a recognisable person or object, introduce one consequence, then leave the final choice unresolved. Fictional dates and interfaces are scenario details. Facts must be separately sourced; use a small persistent POSSIBLE FUTURE label, never a news-like breaking banner.
effort: 60–120 minutes asset production and edit; no audio included.
protocol: Produce original story assets, review factual grounding, verify every future claim is conditional or explicitly fictional, then inspect continuity and safe zones. No real-world experiment outcome is claimed.
evidenceRequirements: Verify current passkey and digital-ID support; universal adoption is speculative.
